newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P puts eight Thai banks on negative watch.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P puts eight Thai banks on negative watch.

text.p: Credit ratings agency Standard & Poors Corp said on Friday it had placed the ratings of eight financial institutions from Thailand on negative creditwatch.

S&P said it had placed the ratings of Bangkok Bank Public Co Ltd, Bank of Asia Public Public Co Ltd, Bank of Ayudhya Public Co Ltd, The Industrial Finance Corp. of Thailand, Krungthai Thanakit Public Co Ltd, Siam Commercial Bank Public Co, Phatra Thanakit Public Co and Thai Farmers Bank Public Co on credit watch negative.
"The rating actions reflect Standard & Poor's concerns that non-performing loans and loan losses will rise to levels not consistent with current ratings," S&P said.

"In addition, the ratings of IFCT and KTT (Krungthai Thanakit), which benefit from their ownership by and relationship with the government, are impacted by the Kingdom of Thailand's negative creditwatch placement," S&P said.

"While rated institutions remain among the best placed of Thai financial institutions in raising provisions to cover rising problem loans, profitability of all Thai financial institutions will be squeezed by higher provisioning."
S&P said the higher than expected asset quality problems were due to;
* the fall out from a deteriorating property market, which government initiatives were not expected to lessen much,
* no imminent expectation of easing interest rates,
* exchange losses from the Thai baht's devaluation,
* support initiatives introduced by the Bank of Thailand not having had the expected stabilising effect on the sector,
* the Thai economic downturn escalating non-performing loans.

The ratings agency said nonaccrual loans in Thailand were very high by international standards and this leading indicator suggested non-performing loans would peak at a higher level than expected by both individual financial institutions and regulators.
"Standard & Poors is reviewing the individual position of each rated financial institution to determine the impact of the expected higher asset quality problems," it said.
